# feat(db): tenant-context boundary — shard 1a (A1/A2 foundation)

<!-- Generated by SessionEnd hook from a commit matching a journal-worthy pattern.
     Next session: review, then promote to a real journal entry OR delete. -->

**Commit**: `f2d85e3eaec0` — feat(db): tenant-context boundary — shard 1a (A1/A2 foundation)

**Body**:

Adds src/sequor/db/tenant_context.py: one boundary helper that binds a session
to an authenticated tenant by setting BOTH halves of the multi-tenant security
model from the same tenant id — the per-tenant AES key (A1 encryption, via
set_tenant_key) AND the PostgreSQL RLS GUC app.current_tenant (A2 isolation).
This is the shared plumbing the A1 column-encryption (1b) and A2 RLS (1c) shards
both build on: the connection boundary that carries tenant identity into the DB.

Design:
- Process-wide KeyManager singleton (get_key_manager) so the LRU key cache is
  shared across call sites, instead of each site constructing its own KeyManager.
- GUC set with is_local=true (SET LOCAL) so it is transaction-scoped and cannot
  leak to the next checkout of a pooled connection — the invariant RLS isolation
  depends on (verified by test_guc_is_transaction_local_not_pool_leaking).
- KeyManager/set_tenant_key resolved via module attribute at call time so Tier-1
  callers mocking the boundary keep working.

Consolidates 2 of the 5 duplicated inline key-load sites (compliance.erase +
onboarding.signup). The 3 onboarding/app.py sites (login, backfill) fold in with
their own shards: login with R7-01 (1e, auth redesign), backfill with 1b.

Sequor is raw SQLAlchemy by design (DEVIATIONS.md § Architecture note); the
framework-first advisory is the known recurring one, not a per-edit defect.

Verified vs sequor-test-pg (pgvector:pg16): integration 39 passed / 1 xfailed
(3 new boundary tests); unit 437 passed (normal env). Known pre-existing:
test_compliance_erasure is non-deterministic under ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY (mocked
tenants lack a provisioned key) — owned by shard 1b.
